tom_tat: To practice the Way is to "return." What does it mean? That means we must give others the good deeds, while we accept the bad deeds - let go of the small self to achieve the great
noi_dung:
I. Cultivation

Cultivating the Way requires "to return." What does it mean? That means we must give others the good deeds, while we accept the bad deeds - letting go of the small self to achieve the great self.

Don't develop hostility toward demons. See them as wise men who assist you in your teachings.

From countless eons until now, from life to life, each person's karma is not the same, so false thoughts are also not the same. Heavy karma leads to many delusions, light karma leads to few delusions.

Cultivators must practice the Way to cut off the cycle of birth and death, to save Sentient Beings, not to seek enlightenment.

People cultivating the Way must always reflect back the light, and should not seek outwards. You can't get it by looking outside, returning to your own nature is complete.

For those who have just begun to practice, the biggest obstacle when applying effort is the greed for lust between men and women. This is the most basic problem.

People who practice the Way should pay attention! Do not sow polluted fate with others. This impure bondage will cause us to fall.

Right now we are fortunate to have a human body. If you don't know how to use your human body to practice, when will you wait to practice? I'm just afraid that when I lose this body, even if I want to practice, it will be too late!

To study Buddhism, it is essential to be truthful. Every action, every word, every gesture must be genuine.

At the temple, we must know how to save every item. That:

"Mourning the temple's belongings

Like protecting the eyes."

Not loving or hating is the Middle Way.

What is cultivating the Way? That means following the Middle Way - treating everyone equally, using compassion as the basis, and being careful when acting, not straying into the trap of love.

There is no moral principle. "today practice the Way, tomorrow to become a Buddha." You can't have a well of water with just one hoe. Practicing is grinding a block of iron into a needle. With enough effort, you will naturally achieve it.

The first thing when learning a secret mantra is to have the right mind and sincere intention. If the mind is not righteous, then when studying, any secret mantra will become evil. If the mind is right, then learning the secret mantra will be enlightened.

Ignorance has two accomplices. What are those two accomplices? That is, greed for food and lust. Both of these things help ignorance create countless bad karma.

There is a saying:

"When you want to be a good person, karma will appear.

When you want to become a Buddha, ghosts come to challenge you."

If you don't want to be a good person, karma won't come. The more determined you are to be a good person, the more karma will come, demanding that you pay off your debt for transparency.

Buddha and demons are only different in one thought--Buddha has a compassionate mind, while demons have a competitive mind.

People who truly know how to practice practice, every move and every move is a practice.

People who practice the Way should not go everywhere advertising their practice. Whoever often advertises his practice will definitely fall into the path of evil.

People cultivating the Tao anywhere must hide and erase their identity, and should not reveal it.

Our mind often resides in other places, not in our own mind. "Residing in other places" means having a body but not a mind.

Preaching the Sutras and preaching the Dharma is cultivating Wisdom. Sitting in Meditation is cultivating Concentration. Not saying nonsense is cultivating the Precepts.

"Affliction is Bodhi." If you know how to use it, affliction is Bodhi. If you don't know how to use it, Bodhi turns into trouble.

Cultivating the Way requires practicing foolishness. The more "foolish" is, the better. "Foolish" to the point where you don't know anything, then false thoughts will no longer exist.

Ignorance means not understanding clearly. The root of ignorance is craving.

The main purpose of practice is to cut off the stream of birth and death, not to seek enlightenment.

To practice, you need to keep yourself pure, like keeping your eyes clear of a grain of sand.

Gambling creates heavy karma. Giving alms accumulates merit. Sitting in meditation eliminates ignorance and gives birth to wisdom.

Practitioners should be careful of what they say in crowded places and guard their minds when sitting alone. Don't talk too much when in public. When alone, you should guard against selfishness and delusion. That way, you will soon be able to single-mindedly see your mind clearly.

Feeling suffering ends suffering.

When you enjoy the blessings, the blessings will end.

People who truly practice the Way must consider all their own actions and movements. Walk, stand, lie down, sit, don't leave mindfulness. Don't be like a mirror - only knowing how to look at other people's faces but not looking at your own true face.

If there is still an attachment, it is an ordinary person's mind. If there is no attachment, that is the mind of the Way.

If you want to not die, you must live like someone who has died - that is, you must keep yourself free from greed, anger, and delusion.

People who study the Way must make vows. The power of prayer has the ability to motivate oneself to practice according to the Right Path, not to go astray. But making a vow without practicing it is like a tree having flowers but not bearing fruit, it's useless!

Using your tongue to preach the Dharma accumulates merit. Also using the tongue but saying bad things creates bad karma. Instead of preaching the Dharma, saying nonsense and gossiping is creating twelve thousand sinful karma.

People who practice the Way often use loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity toward those inside and outside, old, young, big, small, high-ranking, low-ranking, and equanimous, and response will naturally arise.

Cultivating the Way means practicing sincerely and practically. There should be a saying: "If the heart is sincere, it will be flexible."

We live in this world and must always do good deeds. Every breath and strength must be done to accumulate virtue. In this life, you should not rely on the good roots you have planted in previous lives to enjoy all the blessings.

Buddha can transform all Sentient Beings into Dharma weapons, so there is a saying: "Borrow the fake to practice the real thing. This stinky leather bag is just a temporary house." We stay in this house to practice the Way, which means borrowing "the house" our temporary fake body to cultivate into the true Dharma body.

If your mind is filled with greed and does not know enough, then in the future you will fall into hell. If you have too much anger in your mind, always angry from morning to night, you will become a hungry ghost. If you have a heavy stupid mind and only do stupid things, you will turn into an animal.

The biggest weakness of Sentient Beings is delusion--living day and night in delusion, unable to let go. If you can turn your lustful mind into a mind to practice Buddha Dharma, every hour and minute without forgetting to practice, you will quickly become a Buddha.

A truly enlightened person never says he is enlightened. A saint in this world absolutely does not reveal the truth. All those who claim to be Buddha or Bodhisattva are all evil spirits.

People are virtuous not because of their status or age, but through their discreet and silent actions, they naturally reveal their unique Chapter, making others respect them. Chapter in this particular way does not make others afraid, because if they were afraid, they would stay away.

Everyone has three troublesome enemies; that is greed, anger, ignorance. We do not need to eliminate them but transform them into Bodhi seeds.

tom_tat: A practitioner must cultivate the form of selflessness, cultivating to the point where there is no longer any "self." If there is no "I" left, then we can patiently endure everything, no matter what realm comes to our mind, we will not be moved. We consider ourselves as an illusion.
noi_dung:
II. Precepts, Patience

A practitioner must cultivate the form of selflessness, cultivating to the point where there is no longer the "ta.". If there is no longer the "ta", then they can endure everything, no matter the realm, the mind will not be moved, considering themselves like nothingness.

Becoming a Buddha is not easy! If you don't cut off your desire to become a Buddha, you will never be able to achieve it. Most people today like to pray for luck, take shortcuts, and are easily fascinated by magical and strange things; Therefore, he is fascinated and lost in the ghost's net.

Why lie? Because I'm afraid of losing my rights and being disadvantaged.

If you break the precepts of lust, you can easily break the precepts of killing, stealing, and lying. Therefore, the precepts of lust include the precepts of killing, stealing, and lying.

If you keep the Five Precepts and do the Ten Good Deeds, you will be born in the heavenly or human worlds. If you still have a mind of greed, anger, and ignorance, you will fall into several evil paths.

If you clearly understand the Precepts, you can penetrate the entire Buddha Dharma world. If you do not understand the Precepts, you are like clouds flying in the sky, floating in limbo, without a basic support.

The basis of the Precepts is only one thing: non-selfishness.

Effortlessly maintaining the Precepts is mainly in places where no one can see you. Not only must we diligently maintain the Precepts in front of others, but when we are alone we must also always be diligent, diligent, and strictly maintain the Precepts.

When we study Buddhism, we learn not to harm others. As Buddhists, one should be vegetarian; Because eating meat means harming the lives of other Sentient Beings.

Being vegetarian means having to suffer a disadvantage because you cannot enjoy the delicious things in life. But if you are not a vegetarian but eat animal meat, then after death you must go to the underworld to pay your debts. I use my conscience to tell you the truth: If people did not crave " pleasure, " did not crave enjoyment, then after death they would not have to go to court!

A person who studies Buddhism but does not keep the Precepts is like a bottomless vase - as much water is poured in, as much water flows out. Therefore, we must strictly maintain the Precepts and gradually reach the state of anasrava.

No matter what method we practice, we need to have patience to achieve success. If you do not have patience, you cannot achieve success in any method.

What religion do people practice? Cultivate the Way of Patience.

Rings are priceless pearls that people don't know how to find. If you know how to use it, all things will be good.

People cultivating the Way need to endure what others cannot endure, tolerate what others cannot tolerate, wear what others cannot wear - in general, receive what others cannot receive.

When we cultivate the Way, the most important thing is not to fight. "Don't compete" means don't compete with others over what's wrong, good or bad points, or argue about what's right or wrong about others.

No matter what the circumstances are, we should not be overly greedy. You must always know enough and be patient. That is the ultimate wonderful dharma that everyone forgets! Therefore, if you do not fight or are greedy, your blessings will be boundless. If there is still conflict, greed, and chaos, then a lot of bad karma will come to you, and even if you want to escape the three realms, there is no way to escape.

tom_tat: Why don't we recognize our true roots and faces? That's because we haven't gotten rid of our ego and selfishness
noi_dung:
III. Meditation, Buddha Recitation

Why don't we recognize our true roots and faces? That's because we haven't gotten rid of our ego and selfishness.

Meditation means contemplation. What contemplation? Contemplating Prajna. In each thought, let us reflect on ourselves, not on others - reflect on whether we are there or not.

People who meditate must thoroughly understand basic issues. What are those things? That means my bad habits. When we visit the Meditation Hall, we try to eliminate all our bad habits and mistakes.

In the Zen Hall, everyone sits and meditates. That is to test who can pass the exam to Buddhahood. How to get admission? It is necessary to "not accept body and mind inside, not to see the world outside."

Many people who practice Zen commit two shortcomings: the first is deportment, the second is drowsiness - if they do not give rise to false thoughts, they will still fall asleep in the Zen hall.

When meditating, it is important to have patience and perseverance. The secret to meditation is patience. If you can't bear it anymore, still try to be patient. Patience to the extreme will naturally lead to insight, clarity, and enlightenment.

When meditation reaches maturity, not only will delusions disappear, but anger will also subside, afflictions will gradually subside, the Chapter will become more noble, and the spirit will become stronger.

Why are we not in agreement with the Tao? Because the crazy mind has not stopped.

Meditation requires patience, because that is the capital of enlightenment.

When we meditate, we have the opportunity to become enlightened, our self-nature becomes clear like spring returning to the earth, all things proliferate.

A person who truly meditates is a person who truly recites Buddha's name. A person who is truly mindful of Buddha is also a person who is truly practicing Zen. Those who truly observe the Precepts are also those who truly practice Zen.

What is the true self? That means self-nature, also means becoming a Buddha. Becoming a Buddha is the true self. Before becoming Buddha, everything was fake.

Whoever's body is not polluted is a Buddha; Whoever's body is contaminated is a Sentient Beings. What is contamination? In short, "contaminated" means you can't see clearly, you can't let go, and every hour, every moment, every moment gives rise to false thoughts.

If we work hard until we are mature, we will eat without knowing we are eating, wear without being attached to the clothes we are wearing, let alone the things outside the body - all of which we let go!

Cultivation is not just limited to meditating and chanting Sutras. You must practice depending on the place and time. Don't make too many distinctions in your mind. Do not fight for your rights, gain leadership positions to dictate to others, and do not perform or show off your talents in front of your teacher.

Precious morality is the most specialized. A general's talent comes from strategy, not from courage. Soldiers need elite, not many.

Truly reciting Buddha's name is always reciting every second and every minute; There are no false thoughts or thoughts about eating or drinking - if you forget everything, then that is true recitation of Buddha's name.

We recite Buddha's name, Buddha also recites ours--like sending a telegram to Amitabha Buddha. That's called touching the Tao. If we do not recite the Buddha's name, the Buddha has no way to receive it; Therefore, we must recite the Buddha's name.

Reciting the Mantra must be recited until the Mantra flows out from the mind and enters back into the mind. Mantra and mind, mind and Mantra merge into one sound, indistinguishable. Reciting without reciting, reciting without reciting.

We pay homage to the Buddha, and the Buddha accepts the offering, then our blessings and wisdom increase. Therefore, paying homage to Buddha is "feeling,"receiving ceremony is "responding"; That is the Tao.

tieu_de: IV. Happiness of People Leaving Home
tom_tat: Only four people must become monks and live together in harmony to be called the Sangha. That is "harmony and coexistence," without conflict or dispute. A monastic living alone cannot be called
noi_dung:
IV. The Conduct of Monasticism

Only four people must become monks and live together in harmony to be called the Sangha. That is "harmony and coexistence, " is neither disputed nor disputed. A monastic living alone cannot be called a Sangha.

Monastics must solemnly maintain the four postures--walking, standing, lying down, and sitting. Should say: "Walk as light as the wind, sit as steady as a bell, stand as straight as a pine tree, lie down like a bow and arrow."

It is impossible to want the dharma of the world to be the same as the dharma of the world at the same time. I can't stand on two boats - one heading to Giang Bac, the other heading to Giang Nam.

You often know that the Venerable and High Monks of ancient times all attained enlightenment while practicing asceticism. None of the Patriarchs became enlightened while enjoying themselves - a search in the Tripitaka did not reveal any such person.

What must be the criteria for selecting an Abbot? The prerequisite is to not be angry, to know how to treat people with peace, to have good relationships with people everywhere, not to use authority to oppress others, to have a democratic consciousness, making people respectful and respectful.

Monastics can receive offerings, but must not seek offerings. Not being greedy for offerings is the true disciple of Buddha.

The two monastic disciples, Bhikkhus and Bhiksunis, should not strive for fame or position, but should have the spirit of replacing Sentient Beings to suffer and must have an egalitarian mind to help all Sentient Beings.

If a monastic person does not diligently practice Meditation, practice Concentration, recite Sutras, maintain Mantras, strictly follow the Precepts, and only rely on Buddha to get a piece of food and clothing, he will certainly fall into the three evil paths.

"If you have abundant energy, you won't feel cold.

If you have good energy, you won't feel hungry.

If you have full divine power, you won't feel tired."

Tinh, qi, and spirit are the three treasures. People who become monks must cultivate spirit, energy, and spirit.

Monastics must set an example for lay people - if they cannot set a good example, then lay people will not have deep trust, and cannot influence them at all. Therefore, to be a monk, one must have the appearance of a monk.

A person who is a monk must have right knowledge and right view. If you do not have right knowledge and right view, you will definitely stray into the path of demons and be dragged along by fifty skandhas.

Monastics must work together, not create strange things on their own, do whatever they want.

"Specialization is flexible.

Dispersion is hindered."

What do you specialize in the most? That means being single-minded in cutting off desires and eliminating craving. If you don't cut off desires and eliminate cravings, even if you become a monk and practice the Way for eighty thousand eons, you still won't succeed. Therefore, this is very important.

We must always cultivate the Way and cultivate virtue. When our virtues are full and our practice is complete, then we are worthy of being considered a monk.

Monastics must make propagating the Dharma their career.

Propagating Buddha Dharma is the duty and responsibility of us monastics. Therefore, in every thought we must always propagate Buddha Dharma; and every action and gesture is teaching Dharma to Sentient Beings.

tieu_de: V. Cause and Effect, Repentance & Transformation
tom_tat: We are led by karma to be born in this world to suffer the karma of our previous lives. In the past we created different karma, so today we receive different results. Should
noi_dung:
V. Cause and Effect, Repentance & Transformation

"Can't handle karma."

We are led by karma to be born in this world to suffer the karma of our previous lives. In the past we created different karma, so today we receive different results. Should say:

"The net of karma is entangled."

In Chinese, the word "shame" ( , meaning meat) includes a person being eaten and a person who is eating. The person eating is outside and is still human. The person who is eaten turns into an animal. The one who is eating and the one being eaten are linked to each other and cannot be resolved; They keep killing each other over and over again.

If we really want to detoxify the world, everyone must become vegetarian, not eat meat.

The ancients said: "The gentleman creates his own life." Moral people, righteous gentlemen, can change their destiny, going beyond the circle of fate.

Why is there no good? Just because the mind is not good. If you plant evil causes, you will naturally reap evil consequences. If you can correct your evil nature and do good deeds, then good things will come and bad things will fade away.

Bad habits are difficult to break; However, if one can give it up, one truly has the power of Concentration.

"The one who sees my mistakes is my Teacher."

The one who tells us our mistakes is our Good-Knowledge; Therefore, we should be grateful, not resentful.

A respectful mind can transform a strong nature into a gentle and gentle nature.

Worshiping the Buddha means worshiping the Buddha's own nature--worshiping the Buddha in your own nature. To become a Buddha in the future means to become a Buddha by your own nature.

Why do we have evil karma?

Because in the past life, we refused to listen to the teachings and advice of the wise and wise people, and kept running after false thoughts, creating evil karma. That's why this life is often bound by demonic karma, everything is unsatisfactory and unsatisfying.

tom_tat: Nowadays, people go to school just for fame and fortune. The pronunciation of the two words ming li ( ) and fame and fortune ( ) in Chinese is almost the same (ming li), but the meaning is up to 100,000 different.
noi_dung:
VI. Education

Nowadays, people go to school just for fame and fortune. The pronunciation of the two words ming li ( ) and fame and fortune ( ) in Chinese is almost the same (ming li), but the meanings are 108,000 miles different!

Children are like young trees growing - their branches grow so thickly that they need to be pruned before they can become useful material in the future.

Young people! Do you know what the basics of being human are? Those are the eight virtues of filial piety, kindness, loyalty, trust, politeness, righteousness, integrity, and shame.

Why is the world today full of crimes committed by teenagers? Because parents only give birth to children, not care for or educate them.

Our greed is a bottomless pit--higher than the sky, thicker than the earth, deeper than the sea, forever unfillable.

People who are not virtuous are truly poor people.

If someone seeks the Dharma from me, I will tell him or her to eat less, wear less, and sleep less; because:

"If you wear less, your blessings will increase.

Eating less increases longevity,

Sleeping less increases your fortune."

People do not live for food, but live to benefit society, bless the people, and support the world. People must:

Instead, Heaven brought compassion and taught Sentient Beings.

A loyalty to the country and saving the people.

In my life, I've never been busy with myself, never paid attention to this bag of rotten meat.

Why is the world becoming more and more corrupt? Because everyone is fighting - fighting for fame, fighting for profit, fighting for power, fighting for status, and most seriously, fighting for lust.

I want to ask you for the greatest gift--your anger, ignorance, afflictions, and anger.

Natural disasters are not nature causing accidents or nature having accidents, but are disasters we humanity must endure. Human disasters are self-created and self-inflicted.

If we want to develop Buddhism, where should we start? In my opinion, if you want to develop Buddhism, you must first start with education. If children start with education, they will clearly understand Buddhism; When they grow up, they will naturally help Buddhism develop widely.

Doing ghost work is ghost work.

Doing human work means being human.

Doing Buddha's work means being Buddha.

tom_tat: Sentient Beings in the present are our parents in the past, Buddhas in the future. If anger arises towards Sentient Beings, it means anger towards parents and Buddhas, becoming a disobedient, unruly child.
noi_dung:
VII. Buddhism & Buddhism

Principles of Buddhism are that everyone can become a Buddha.

Sentient Beings in the present are our parents in the past, Buddhas in the future. If anger arises towards Sentient Beings, it means anger towards parents and Buddhas, becoming a disobedient and unfilial child.

I call Buddhism the religion of Sentient Beings, because everyone cannot escape from nothingness, the Dharma-world, everyone is Sentient Beings. Therefore, Buddhism is the religion of all Sentient Beings.

I also call Buddhism the religion of people, because everyone has the qualifications to become Buddha. As long as we practice diligently, everyone will surely become a Buddha in the end.

I call Buddhism the religion of the mind, because everyone has a mind. Practicing practice means eliminating deep delusions and preserving the true mind - having a false mind is an ordinary person, having a true mind is a Buddha.

Lust is the source of birth and death. If you don't cut off lust, you won't be able to be born in heaven, let alone attain the unsurpassed Bodhisattva path? Therefore, if you want to practice Samadhi Meditation, if you want to overcome the sea of ​​birth and death and suffering, you must first pass through this barrier.

If you want to develop the mind of Bodhi, you must listen and study Buddha Dharma a lot. When you clearly understand Buddha Dharma, you will naturally develop the mind of Bodhi.

Buddhism covers all of space, the Dharma world. All Sentient Beings have full Buddha-nature and can become Buddhas. If you do not believe in Buddha Dharma now, you will believe in the future. If you still do not believe in Buddha Dharma in the future, you will believe in the next life. Not only will you definitely believe in Buddha Dharma, but you will also definitely become Buddhas!

The Shurangama Mantra is the king among Mantras, and is also the longest. This mantra is very important to the rise and fall of Buddhism. In the world, if there are still people who recite the Shurangama Mantra, the Dharma will still exist. If there were no more people reciting the Shurangama Mantra, there would be no Dharma.

The Shurangama Mantra is a mantra proclaimed by the Tathagata's incarnation from the light above the Buddha's crown - therefore, its wonderful uses are inconceivable, each word contains so many wonderful and profound uses.

During the End of the Dharma, all the pagan demons, evil spirits, ghosts, ghosts, ghosts, mountain and river monsters, etc. were most afraid of the Shurangama uncle. The Shurangama Mantra is the mantra that " destroys evil and manifests righteousness."

During the Dharma era, everyone wanted to practice. During the Dharma Ending Age, everyone did not practice. If everyone practices, the Ending Dharma will become the True Dharma.

What is Buddha Dharma? In short, Buddha Dharma is the key. Presently teaching the Sutra means teaching about this key. Presently preaching the Dharma means preaching about this key. This is the key to wisdom that opens the lock of ignorance.

Buddha Dharma is still in the world. If we can bravely overcome the crazy waterfall, develop a great Bodhi mind, and sincerely and earnestly practice the Buddha Dharma, then we still have a chance to escape from the Saha world. On the contrary, we keep spinning in the six paths without stopping, forever unable to escape suffering in this world.

tom_tat: How to eliminate anger caused by ignorance? You must practice the method of Patience and Humility, and you absolutely should not get angry. This is the most important thing. If you don't give rise to anger, wisdom will arise
noi_dung:
VIII. Wisdom

Merit and impartiality is the Dharma.

Selfishness and self-interest are evil.

How to eliminate anger caused by ignorance? You must practice the method of Patience and Humility, and you absolutely should not get angry. This is the most important thing. If you do not give rise to anger, wisdom will arise.

In the Dharma Ending Age, everyone made the common mistake of being too arrogant, using their ears instead of their eyes. When they heard something good, they immediately ran after it.

We, those who believe in Buddha, should not be overly superstitious, but need to get rid of superstition. What is superstition? It is crazy belief, believing immediately what others have just said, believing blindly.

Why are Sentient Beings crazy? Because of mistaking ignorance as the master of the house, wisdom is thrown away. Ignorance gives orders: "For what is right is wrong; for wrong to be right."

From meditation, purifying thoughts, eliminating desires, causing wisdom to arise.

People who often like to get angry are mostly stupid, deeply ignorant, and do not have the slightest amount of effort to cultivate.

False thoughts are false thoughts, neither true nor real. People who always have crazy delusions are people who know clearly that something is not right but still try to do it and cunningly argue that it is right.

If you regularly reflect back the light, clearly see your own nature, and constantly give birth to Prajna Wisdom, then that is creating merit. Applying the Wisdom of Prajna everywhere, transforming without end, without being contaminated in advance, without creating impure things, is creating virtue.

In fact, the Prajnaparamita Wisdom of the foolish and the wise is not inherently different. The difference is that stupid people don't know how to use wisdom, while wise people know how to use it.

If there are no internal or external attachments, " comes" and "go" can both be free and independent, knowing where they came from and where they are going. "To" can be said to return--to return to one's body and mind. "Going" means going to the Dharma world.

If you are attached to " coming and going, " then you will be hindered and unable to be free.

If you have "tri" you will be like the sun, if you have "hue" you will be like the moon.

The hope of being enlightened or the hope of becoming a Buddha are all delusions. Everyone must remember: Only seek practice, not false hope.

If a Bodhisattva has supernatural powers but does not manifest them, then what is the use of having supernatural powers?

Bodhisattvas use supernatural powers to educate Sentient Beings, like building a tree to see images, causing Sentient Beings to increase their faith. Thus, there are two-way benefits. That is the method of skillful means.

Please pay attention! Demons also show supernatural powers, causing those who are greedy for magical powers and do not have the power of concentration to fall into the trap, lose their Tao, and become relatives of demons. Regarding this point, everyone must pay special attention and cannot help but be careful!

Anyone who wants to have magical powers must first let go of all things and concentrate on pure meditation. When your practice is ripe, you will naturally have magical powers. Divine power is not something that can be sought from the outside, but can only be obtained when one realizes it within.

"Seeing through, letting go, being at ease."Seeing through means understanding the problem clearly. Letting go means liberation. Only when liberation is achieved can there be true freedom.

To study Buddhism, you need to use wisdom, not emotions. Using wisdom to study Buddha Dharma is the Dharma. Using emotions to learn Buddha Dharma is the end of Dharma.

Many people think that human life is joy. In fact, those joys are all fake. True joy must be found within one's own nature, not from the outside.

tom_tat: Why are all humans in a state of confusion? That's because they don't understand where they come from or where they go when they die. Every day, the figure you see when you look in the mirror is you. If you want to know your original face (true mind)…
noi_dung:
French

Why are all humans in a state of confusion? That's because they don't understand where they come from or where they go when they die. Every day, the figure you see when you look in the mirror is you. If you want to know your original face (true mind), you must turn around and look inside, find your own mind. People in this world are confused by the five desires, day by day they are oppressed by money, beauty, fame, food, drink, and sleep to the point of suffocation and difficulty breathing, but they still want to willingly volunteer to be slaves to those things.

My greed is higher than the sky, thicker than the earth. It's like a bottomless bucket, no matter how much stuff you put in, it won't be full.

People without morality are truly poor.

Where can I find the pearls and jewels that I already have? Look for it in the Avatamsaka Sutra. There is a saying: Without reading the Avatamsaka Sutra, you cannot know the wealth of the Buddhas. The Avatamsaka Sutra is the king of all kings of scriptures (ie the top sutra of the most wonderful sutras that Buddha preached).

If you use greed, anger and ignorance to handle everything, the result will be gloomy heaven and earth, causing all sorts of disasters. If we use precepts, concentration and wisdom to solve problems, heaven and earth will be clear and everything will be auspicious. It should be said: Where there are many evil people, there are many accidents; Wherever there are many good people, that place is always happy. Accidents and peace are all caused by people.

People don't become Buddhas because they keep putting effort into the mouth (talking without cultivating, not practicing).

Everything, everything is Buddha Dharma, it is something that cannot be attached to, cannot be grasped. In the world, all things, all things, whatever happens is preaching the Dharma (exposing the truth), it is preaching the sutras.
